newsitem.title: SUDAN: Rebels abduct relief workers in Sudan - official.
newsitem.headline: Rebels abduct relief workers in Sudan - official.

text.p: Rebels from a southern Sudanese group that signed a peace deal with the Khartoum government this year have kidnapped two government relief workers, a Sudanese official said.
Mohammed Ramatallah, commissioner general for humanitarian relief, was quoted by the official Sudanese news agency SUNA, on Sunday as saying the rebels seized the two men on September 25.

"The two workers, a relief worker and a radio operator, were abducted while they were on duty delivering relief aid between al-Renk and Malakal in Upper Nile state in southern Sudan," Ramatallah said.
He said the rebels were loyal to Lam Akol, who heads a dissident faction of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
The splinter group, SPLA United, signed in May a peace charter with the government that Khartoum hopes will end more than 10 years of war between its army and the mostly Christian and animist south.
It is not clear why the rebels abducted the government relief workers.

Ramatallah urged United Nations officials who oversee relief work in the south to secure the immediate release of the abducted workers and to ensure the free flow of relief supplies to the affected areas.
